messages.subject: cut points in the algorithm?
parts:
Hi -
I'm new to using GGIR, new to processing accelerometery data, and not all proficient in R. I've been reading the papers that are referenced on the GGIR website (and some of the papers that those papers reference) and I'm having a difficult time identifying exactly what the algorithm is doing and what cut-points are being applied. I've also looked through GGIR documentation and I can't find the information there either. 
I usually use SAS and I'm accustomed to being able to see what's actually happening in the background say in a macro, but I find that R documentation provides only general comments about steps and does not include detail such as the equations. Is this impression correct? 
I'm hoping someone can point me to the actual algorithms and detailed documentation on GGIR that would be more similar to a SAS macro's documentation. I want to understand the algorithm, perhaps make a SAS version (since I am helpless when it comes to troubleshooting in R, but have been using SAS for a decade), and also understand from exactly where it came from (the decision tree from the Zhang 2012 paper??? but this paper does not report it's cut-points either) to get a better understanding of the validation sample (I'm concerned they may be quite different from our cohort of mid-life cancer survivors). 
Any help would be much appreciated. 
Cheers, 

Kim

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] cut points in the algorithm?
parts:
Hi Kim,

All GGIR source code is available here: https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR. All functions are documented: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/GGIR.pdf

GGIR facilitates a variety of ways to apply cut-points, so there is not one but multiple places where cut-points applied:
- In GGIR part 2 cut-points are used to estimate time in MVPA per 24 hours, but based on six different algorithm using a variety of epoch lengths and both with and without consider bouts. This happens in function g.analyse.perday, lines 513 - 545, note that g.getbout, is called to do the bout detection.
- In GGIR part 5 cut-points are used in a more elaborate way, detecting also inactivity and light activity during the waking hours of a day. Here, the action happens in function identify_levels, and as you will see this function also calls the g.getbout function. 

Best, Vincent
